phase_1.title: Phase 1 · SKS-45 Trigger Release & Ignition Drive
phase_1.description: Pulling the trigger disengages the sear, freeing the spring-driven hammer or striker to impact the 7.62×39mm M43 primer.

phase_2.title: Phase 2 · 355 MPa Chamber Pressure Rise
phase_2.description: The propellant charge ignites inside the locked chamber, driving peak pressure to 355 MPa while sealing the cartridge case against the breech.

phase_3.title: Phase 3 · 520 mm Barrel Engraving & Acceleration
phase_3.description: The projectile engages the 4-groove bore and accelerates to 735 m/s (2130 J).

phase_4.title: Phase 4 · Bolt Tilt Unlock & Operating Impulse
phase_4.description: Once chamber pressure decays safely, carrier cam ramps lift the tilting bolt tail clear of the receiver locking shoulder for extraction.

phase_5.title: Phase 5 · Spent Case Extraction & Ejection
phase_5.description: The extractor pulls the fired brass clear of the chamber and pivots it out the ejection port while the recoil spring compresses.

phase_6.title: Phase 6 · Next-Round Stripping & Breech Lockup
phase_6.description: Driven forward by the recoil spring, the breech strips the next round from the 10-round supply and locks solidly into battery.

phase_7.title: Phase 7 · Disconnector Handoff & Sear Reset
phase_7.description: Releasing the trigger hands control cleanly back to the primary sear, leaving the SKS-45 staged for its 35–40 RPM practical (semi-auto · 10-rd stripper clip) cadence.

zh.headline: 西蒙诺夫 SKS-45 半自动卡宾枪：1945 年机械传奇与工程剖析
zh.deck: 谢尔盖·西蒙诺夫设计的 SKS-45 是首批发射 7.62×39mm M43 中间威力弹的军用卡宾枪，以短行程分体式活塞推杆、整锻铣削机匣、下倾闭锁枪机与 10 发顶部桥夹固定弹仓著称，至今仍作为多国三军仪仗队礼宾用枪。 本馆以 1:1 真实工程比例重现其 20 大核心构件与完整工作循环。

acts.title: 时代召唤与研发立项：SKS-45 的诞生背景
paragraphs: 1945 年问世的 西蒙诺夫 SKS-45 半自动卡宾枪 由苏联图拉兵工厂（Tula Arsenal）主导研制，定位为经典的半自动卡宾枪。尽管很快在苏军主力定位上让位于 AK-47，SKS 及其中国 56 式半自动步枪衍生型全球产量超过 1,500 万支，至今依然是仪仗礼兵最具辨识度的经典礼枪。
谢尔盖·西蒙诺夫设计的 SKS-45 是首批发射 7.62×39mm M43 中间威力弹的军用卡宾枪，以短行程分体式活塞推杆、整锻铣削机匣、下倾闭锁枪机与 10 发顶部桥夹固定弹仓著称，至今仍作为多国三军仪仗队礼宾用枪。 整件装备总长 1,020 mm（全木托 · 折叠刺刀位）、空重 3.85 kg，成为同期半自动步枪领域最具辨识度的里程碑之一。
acts.audioScript: 第一幕，时代起源。1945 年，苏联图拉兵工厂（Tula Arsenal）推出了划时代的西蒙诺夫 SKS-45 半自动卡宾枪。尽管很快在苏军主力定位上让位于 AK-47，SKS 及其中国 56 式半自动步枪衍生型全球产量超过 1,500 万支，至今依然是仪仗礼兵最具辨识度的经典礼枪。 它的核心设计聚焦于分体式短行程活塞与独立复进簧推杆，冲击结束后即脱开枪机框，奠定了其在半自动步枪发展史中的经典地位。
acts.focusPartLabel: 主体机匣与闭锁承力框架

acts.title: 核心机械构造与闭锁奥秘
paragraphs: 西蒙诺夫 SKS-45 半自动卡宾枪 的机械灵魂在于其「短行程导气活塞推杆 · 尾部下倾偏移闭锁与 10 发内置固定弹仓」结构体系。在发射工作循环中，导气机框斜面抬起闭锁块尾部脱离机匣闭锁肩，实现直线抽壳抛壳，将高压能量精确约束于承力框架之内。
制造工艺方面，关键承力件采用发蓝锻钢与油润精选胡桃木/桦木托精加工而成。整锻铣削机匣配敞口顶装 10 发固定弹仓，桥夹一按即满并自带空仓挂机，在严苛实战条件下依然保持顺畅节拍与长期尺寸稳定性。
acts.audioScript: 第二幕，核心机械原理。西蒙诺夫 SKS-45 半自动卡宾枪 采用短行程导气活塞推杆 · 尾部下倾偏移闭锁与 10 发内置固定弹仓。在每个击发周期中，导气机框斜面抬起闭锁块尾部脱离机匣闭锁肩，实现直线抽壳抛壳。借助发蓝锻钢与油润精选胡桃木/桦木托工艺与高强度配合，实现了整锻铣削机匣配敞口顶装 10 发固定弹仓，桥夹一按即满并自带空仓挂机。
acts.focusPartLabel: 高强度闭锁枪机头与抽壳钩

acts.title: 弹道性能、内膛工艺与实战效能
paragraphs: 该平台配用 7.62×39mm M43 弹药规格与 520 mm 镀铬枪管（4 条右旋膛线 · 240 mm 缠距），最高工作膛压约 355 MPa，可赋予弹头 735 m/s 的出膛初速与 2,130 J 动能，有效作用距离达 400 米。
内膛技术特点方面，520 mm 加长枪管比 AK-47 多出 105 mm 加速行程，初速与平直度更佳。同时，520 mm 较长镀铬枪管与全长传统木托赋予极佳持枪指向性与半自动精度，令其在 35–40 发/分（纯半自动 · 10 发桥夹顶部压弹） 的节奏下兼具精准控制与可靠输出。
acts.audioScript: 第三幕，弹道与实战表现。配备 520 毫米身管与 7.62×39mm M43 口径，西蒙诺夫 SKS-45 半自动卡宾枪 实现了每秒 735 米的初速与 400 米有效射程。520 mm 加长枪管比 AK-47 多出 105 mm 加速行程，初速与平直度更佳，展现了卓越的工程平衡。

acts.title: 人机工效、供弹哲学与百年遗产
paragraphs: 围绕 10 发容量的机匣内置固定盒式弹仓与 36 mm 膛轴设计，西蒙诺夫 SKS-45 半自动卡宾枪 将单发后坐冲量控制在 7.9 N·s 水平。底板铰链一拨即可快速倾空未发弹药，保养拆装无需专用工具。
如今在数字兵器库 3D 百年展厅（BAY-44）中，您可以随时通过三轴剖视、100% 爆炸视图与实时运动学滑块，零距离拆解这座跨越时代的机械工程杰作。
acts.audioScript: 第四幕，百年遗产。凭借 10 发容量的机匣内置固定盒式弹仓与出色的整体工效，底板铰链一拨即可快速倾空未发弹药，保养拆装无需专用工具。欢迎在 BAY-44 展位亲手切开剖面、逐件拆解，感受 西蒙诺夫 SKS-45 半自动卡宾枪 的机械魅力。

en.headline: Simonov SKS-45 Carbine: The 1945 Mechanical Legend
en.deck: Sergei Simonov’s SKS-45 was among the first service rifles chambered in 7.62×39mm M43, combining a milled receiver, short-stroke tappet piston, rear-tilting bolt, and hinged 10-round stripper-clip magazine. Preserved in 1:1 interactive 3D CAD scale across all 20 functional assemblies in BAY-44.

acts.title: Origins & Operational Mandate of the SKS-45
paragraphs: Introduced in 1945 by Tula Arsenal in Soviet Union, the Simonov SKS-45 Carbine emerged as a defining Semi-Automatic Carbine. Though superseded in Soviet front-line service by the AK-47, over 15 million SKS carbines and licensed variants (including the Type 56) were produced worldwide, remaining iconic ceremonial rifles.

Sergei Simonov’s SKS-45 was among the first service rifles chambered in 7.62×39mm M43, combining a milled receiver, short-stroke tappet piston, rear-tilting bolt, and hinged 10-round stripper-clip magazine. Measuring 1,020 mm (Full Hardwood Stock) at an unloaded weight of 3.85 kg, it reshaped expectations across the Assault & Battle Rifle class.
acts.audioScript: Act One: Historical Origins. In 1945, Tula Arsenal of Soviet Union introduced the Simonov SKS-45 Carbine. Though superseded in Soviet front-line service by the AK-47, over 15 million SKS carbines and licensed variants (including the Type 56) were produced worldwide, remaining iconic ceremonial rifles. Anchored by its hallmark design trait — Short-stroke piston and spring-loaded op-rod decouple cleanly from the carrier after unlocking — it quickly established an enduring engineering benchmark.

acts.title: Core Operating Architecture & Lockup Mechanics
paragraphs: At the mechanical heart of the Simonov SKS-45 Carbine sits its Short-Stroke Gas Piston & Op-Rod · Tilting Bolt with 10-Round Integral Stripper-Clip Magazine. Throughout every firing cycle, carrier cam ramps lift the tilting bolt tail clear of the receiver locking shoulder for extraction, containing 355 MPa of operating pressure safely.

Constructed in blued forged ordnance steel paired with oil-finished walnut, the assembly achieves durable field tolerances. Notably, Milled receiver with fixed 10-round magazine loads rapidly via stripper clips with last-round hold-open, sustaining dependable operation under severe environmental stress.
acts.audioScript: Act Two: Core Mechanical Architecture. The Simonov SKS-45 Carbine relies on Short-Stroke Gas Piston & Op-Rod · Tilting Bolt with 10-Round Integral Stripper-Clip Magazine. During each cycle, carrier cam ramps lift the tilting bolt tail clear of the receiver locking shoulder for extraction. Machined from blued forged ordnance steel paired with oil-finished walnut, it delivers standout engineering reliability: Milled receiver with fixed 10-round magazine loads rapidly via stripper clips with last-round hold-open.

acts.title: Ballistic Performance, Bore Craft & Range Reach
paragraphs: Chambered for 7.62×39mm M43 with 520 mm Chrome-Lined Barrel (4-Groove RH · 240 mm Twist), the Simonov SKS-45 Carbine develops 735 m/s muzzle velocity and 2,130 J of kinetic energy for effective engagement out to 400 meters.

Internally, 520 mm barrel adds 105 mm over the AK-47 for higher velocity and flatter 400 m trajectory. Combined with its 35–40 RPM practical (semi-auto · 10-rd stripper clip) tempo, 520 mm chrome-lined barrel and classic full-length stock yield crisp semi-auto pointability, delivering disciplined accuracy across demanding field conditions.
acts.audioScript: Act Three: Ballistic Performance. Driving 7.62×39mm M43 through its 520 millimeter bore, the Simonov SKS-45 Carbine achieves 735 meters per second and 400 meters of effective reach. 520 mm barrel adds 105 mm over the AK-47 for higher velocity and flatter 400 m trajectory.

acts.title: Feed Philosophy, Ergonomics & Centennial Legacy
paragraphs: Fed by a 10-round internal fixed box magazine with a 36 mm bore-axis height, the platform manages 7.9 N-s of recoil impulse cleanly. Hinged magazine floorplate dumps unfired rounds instantly for safe administrative clearing.
Now archived in Digital Armory 3D Centennial Gallery (BAY-44), all 20 interactive assemblies can be sectioned live along three axes, exploded to 100%, and inspected part by part.
acts.audioScript: Act Four: Engineering Legacy. Pairing its 10-round internal fixed box magazine with disciplined recoil geometry, Hinged magazine floorplate dumps unfired rounds instantly for safe administrative clearing. Explore BAY-44 in live section cut and exploded disassembly to study every working link of the Simonov SKS-45 Carbine.
